cultural.vision_reason: This shows a traditional Ethiopian devotional painting in the characteristic Amhara/Ethiopian Orthodox style — bold flat colors, large frontal eyes, equestrian warrior saints (St. George/Theodore) spearing prostrate foes, priests with hand crosses — a recognized genre of Amhara church folk art, here on paper rather than parchment/cloth but stylistically authentic.

physical.title: painting
physical.summary:
Painting in water based pigment on printed Italian military paper depicting in the top register, an ethiopian equestrian saint with two dog-faced followers. The saint's horse tramples on a prostrate man. To the right are two priests at the entrance to a church, one carries a hand cross.
The lower register shows Saint Theodore slaying a serpent. The saint rides a horse with Ethiopian toe stirrup and tack and wears a cape (lemd). A small angel appears to the right.

Verso; Saint Victor is shown slaying a white bull. He rides a horse with Ethiopian toe stirrup, elaborate headgear and breast band. To the top right is an angel.
Framed with a paper mount.
